candidates.explanation: The comment says the signing secret embeds the current password hash so that reset links stop verifying once the password changes. The code actually returns forgotSecret + user.email, and the password hash is not included. Changing the password therefore does not change the secret. The same JWT keeps verifying until it expires, so the emailed link can be reused to set another password.

After verifying the hash, the method sets the new password but never invalidates the token. There is no used-token store and no token version. The only single-use protection is the secret derivation, which is broken, so the same link verifies again.

fix.description: Include the user's current password hash in the secret, for example `${forgotSecret}${user.password ?? ''}`, in getForgotSecret. Make sure findById returns the password hash. Both the sign step in forgotPassword and the verify step in resetPassword must use the same value. The token then stops verifying as soon as the password changes. Alternatively, store a one-time token or nonce and delete it after use.
